    // Taubin's lambda/mu smoothing (https://doi.org/10.1145/218380.218473): a
    // shrinking step of `lambda` followed by an inflating step of `mu`. With
    // mu more negative than lambda is positive, the pass band leaves low
    // frequencies alone, so the volume survives where plain Laplacian smoothing
    // eats it.
    TaubinSmoothed(self: TriangleMesh3D, weighting: LaplacianWeighting, lambda: Number, mu: Number, iterations: Integer): TriangleMesh3D
    {
        var topology = self.TopologyOf;
        return Repeat(iterations, 0).Reduce(self, (mesh, step) =>
            mesh.TaubinStep(topology, weighting, lambda, mu));
    }

    // Taubin smoothing at the usual settings: uniform weights, lambda 0.5 and mu
    // -0.53, the pair Taubin's own examples use.
    TaubinSmoothed(self: TriangleMesh3D, iterations: Integer): TriangleMesh3D
        => self.TaubinSmoothed(LaplacianWeighting.UniformWeights, 0.5, -0.53, iterations);

    // A vector normalized, or zero where there is nothing to normalize: an
    // isolated vertex touches no face and therefore has no normal.
    NormalizedOrZero(v: Vector3D): Vector3D
        => v.Magnitude <= 0.0 ? Vector3D(0.0, 0.0, 0.0) : v.Normalize;

    // The area-weighted vertex normal of every vertex: the normalized sum of the
    // vector areas of the incident triangles, which weights each face by its own
    // area without a separate weight term.
    VertexNormalVectors(self: TriangleMesh3D): Array<Vector3D>
        => self.Positions.Count.MapRange(v => NormalizedOrZero(
            self.Faces.Count.MapRange(f => f).Reduce(Vector3D(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), (acc, f) =>
                self.Faces[f].HasVertex(VertexIndex(v))
                    ? acc + self.Triangle(FaceIndex(f)).TwiceVectorArea
                    : acc)));

    // One tangential relaxation step: every interior vertex moves toward the
    // centroid of its ring, with the component along its own normal removed, so
    // the vertices redistribute over the surface without leaving it. This is the
    // step that makes isotropic remeshing produce even triangles rather than
    // merely correctly-sized ones.
    TangentialRelaxationStep(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, strength: Number): TriangleMesh3D
    {
        var neighbors = self.VertexNeighborTable(topology);
        var normals = self.VertexNormalVectors;
        var boundary = self.BoundaryVertexFlags(topology);
        return (self.Positions.Count.MapRange(v =>
                    boundary[v]
                        ? self.Positions[v]
                        : self.Positions[v] + TangentialPart(
                            UniformLaplacian(self.Positions, neighbors, v), normals[v]) * strength),
                self.Faces);
    }

    // The part of a displacement that lies in the plane of a normal.
    TangentialPart(displacement: Vector3D, normal: Vector3D): Vector3D
        => displacement - normal * displacement.Dot(normal);

    // Tangential relaxation, repeated over one shared connectivity.
    TangentiallyRelaxed(self: TriangleMesh3D, strength: Number, iterations: Integer): TriangleMesh3D
    {
        var topology = self.TopologyOf;
        return Repeat(iterations, 0).Reduce(self, (mesh, step) =>
            mesh.TangentialRelaxationStep(topology, strength));
    }

    //==
    // # Quadric error metrics
    //
    // Garland and Heckbert's error quadric
    // (https://doi.org/10.1145/258734.258849) is the sum, over the planes of the
    // faces around a vertex, of the squared distance to each plane — and a sum of
    // squared plane distances IS a quadratic form in homogeneous coordinates.
    // That is exactly the `Quadric` of `spatial-structures.types.plato`, whose
    // `Coefficients` is a symmetric `Matrix4x4`, so no second type is declared
    // here: the surface reading of a `Quadric` is "the points where the form is
    // zero", and the decimation reading is "the value of the form at a point".
    //
    // The plane quadrics are weighted by triangle area, which is the standard
    // practical refinement of the paper's unweighted sum: without it a fan of
    // slivers outvotes the large faces around it.

    // The quadric of one plane: the outer product of its (a, b, c, d) coefficients
    // with itself, whose form at a point is the SQUARED distance to the plane. The
    // Hesse form stores Dot(Normal, p) = Distance, so d is the negated Distance.
    PlaneQuadric(plane: Plane): Quadric
    {
        var n = plane.Normal.Vector;
        var v = Number4(n.X, n.Y, n.Z, 0.0 - plane.Distance);
        return Quadric((v * v.X, v * v.Y, v * v.Z, v * v.W));
    }

    // The area-weighted quadric of one triangle: the quadric of the plane it lies
    // in, scaled by its area. Area weighting is the standard practical refinement
    // of the paper's unweighted sum — without it a fan of slivers outvotes the
    // large faces around it.
    TriangleQuadric(t: Triangle3D): Quadric
        => Quadric(PlaneQuadric(t.FromTriangle).Coefficients * t.Area);

    // The quadric that is zero everywhere: the identity of quadric summation.
    ZeroQuadric(_: Quadric): Quadric
        => Quadric((Number4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0), Number4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
                    Number4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0), Number4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)));

    // Two quadrics summed: the form of the sum is the sum of the forms, which is
    // what makes an edge's quadric the sum of its endpoints'.
    Add(a: Quadric, b: Quadric): Quadric
        => Quadric(a.Coefficients + b.Coefficients);

    // The value of the quadratic form at a point: the accumulated squared distance
    // to the planes the quadric was built from.
    QuadricError(self: Quadric, p: Point3D): Number
    {
        var v = Number4(p.X, p.Y, p.Z, 1.0);
        return v.Transform(self.Coefficients).Dot(v);
    }

    // The point where the quadratic form is smallest, found by solving the 3x3
    // system that sets its gradient to zero. The system is expressed as the
    // quadric with its last COLUMN replaced by (0, 0, 0, 1), whose inverse carries
    // the answer in its translation row. A singular system — a flat or symmetric
    // neighbourhood — has no unique minimum, and the fallback is returned instead.
    QuadricMinimizer(self: Quadric, fallback: Point3D): Point3D
    {
        var q = self.Coefficients;
        var solve = Matrix4x4(
            Number4(q.Row1.X, q.Row1.Y, q.Row1.Z, 0.0),
            Number4(q.Row2.X, q.Row2.Y, q.Row2.Z, 0.0),
            Number4(q.Row3.X, q.Row3.Y, q.Row3.Z, 0.0),
            Number4(q.Row4.X, q.Row4.Y, q.Row4.Z, 1.0));
        return solve.CanInvert ? solve.Invert.Translation.ToPoint : fallback;
    }

    // The error quadric of every vertex: the area-weighted sum over the triangles
    // that use it. Quadratic in vertex count times face count.
    VertexQuadrics(self: TriangleMesh3D): Array<Quadric>
        => self.Positions.Count.MapRange(v => self.Faces.Count.MapRange(f => f)
            .Reduce(Quadric.ZeroQuadric, (q, f) =>
                self.Faces[f].HasVertex(VertexIndex(v))
                    ? q.Add(TriangleQuadric(self.Triangle(FaceIndex(f))))
                    : q));
